record.original_question: Extend the symplectomorphism and Kahler-map properties of the Madelung transform to wave functions that are allowed to vanish, and explain the quantization-condition controversy in momentum-map terms for the relevant semidirect product action.

evidence.quote: Problem 37. Extend the above results on symplectomorphism and the Kähler map to the wave functions with zeros on M . Explain the quantization condition controversy [141, 48] in the language of the momentum map for the above semi-direct product group. 28

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian manifold. Consider the space of complex wave functions $\Psi: M \to \mathbb{C}$ of fixed $L^2$-norm, and the cotangent bundle $T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$ of the space of smooth probability densities on $M$. The Madelung transform $\Psi = \sqrt{\rho}\, e^{i\theta/\hbar}$ is known, on the open set of nowhere-vanishing wave functions, to define (after quotienting by the constant phase $S^1$-action) a symplectomorphism and indeed a Kähler map from this space to $T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$, where the wave-function side carries the Fubini–Study Kähler structure and the density side carries the structure induced by the Fisher–Rao information metric. Moreover, on this regular stratum the inverse Madelung map admits an interpretation as a momentum map for the action of a certain semidirect product group $G \ltimes C^\infty(M, \mathbb{R})$ (the diffeomorphism group acting on smooth functions) on the space of wave functions.

(a) Extend the symplectomorphism and Kähler-map properties of the Madelung transform to the full space of smooth wave functions on $M$, including those that are allowed to vanish on subsets of $M$ (with arbitrary zero set, possibly of positive codimension), giving a precise description of the geometric structures and the regularity needed across the zero locus.

(b) In this extended framework, give a momentum-map interpretation, with respect to the semidirect product group action above, that accounts for the discrepancy in the quantization condition $\oint d\theta \in 2\pi\hbar\,\mathbb{Z}$ around zeros (nodes) of the wave function: explain in momentum-map terms why and when this integrality condition must hold, thereby resolving the controversy over whether the Madelung hydrodynamic formulation requires the phase $\theta$ to be globally single-valued modulo $2\pi\hbar$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Madelung transform has been shown to be a symplectomorphism and Kähler map on the regular stratum (nowhere-vanishing wave functions), with a momentum-map interpretation for a semidirect product group action (Khesin–Misiołek–Modin, and Fusca). The extension to wave functions with zeros, and the momentum-map explanation of the quantization-condition controversy, are posed as open problems and do not appear to have been resolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of the Madelung Transform
status_evidence.snippet: The Madelung transform is a Kähler map (a symplectomorphism and an isometry) between the space of wave functions and the cotangent bundle to the density space.
status_evidence.claim: Kähler-map property established on the open stratum of nowhere-vanishing wave functions.

status_evidence.title: Geometric hydrodynamics via Madelung transform (PNAS)
status_evidence.snippet: Madelung transform between the Schrödinger equation and Newton's equations is a symplectomorphism of the corresponding phase spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Symplectomorphism property known on the regular part; extension to wave functions with zeros not addressed.
